verdict.rationale: First-party docs show LM Studio runs models through `llama.cpp` or the vendor-specific `Apple MLX` engine and exposes a GPU offload control (`lms load --gpu`). Community posts corroborate MLX on Apple Silicon and imply CUDA acceleration on NVIDIA. However, there is no first-party documentation of NVIDIA CUDA or AMD ROCm/Vulkan kernels, and one user reports AMD/Radeon support is not seamless. missing for 10: first-party documentation of NVIDIA CUDA and AMD (ROCm/Vulkan) acceleration backends, a vendor runtime-selection mechanism, and hands-on corroboration on non-Apple GPUs.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run models on NVIDIA, AMD, or other GPU vendors using vendor-specific acceleration kernels

citations.quote: no way to set CUDA acceleration before loading a model
Now that LM Studio supports MLX models, it's one of the most efficient too.
